# Validate metering data schema and define the reporting consumption contract

## Description

This investigation resolves the strategy's open question: the metering data
schema owned by the in-flight GPU usage metering strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990) is
not final, and the chargeback reporting built in this strategy consumes that
data. The outcome determines how per-project GPU-hour reports are computed, so
this must be resolved before the reporting implementation starts.

The deliverable is a validated consumption contract: a written statement of the
metering data fields the reporting work will consume, confirmation of whether
they support the reporting requirements, and a gap list to raise against the
metering strategy if they do not.

## Scope

- Review the current state and draft schema of the GPU usage metering work
  (RHAISTRAT-9990) together with that strategy's owners.
- Determine, with a defined pass/fail criterion, whether the metering data
  provides:
  - per-project attribution of GPU usage (consumption can be attributed to the
    project that used it);
  - accumulable usage quantities expressible as GPU-hours per project;
  - timestamps sufficient to compute totals over administrator-selectable time
    ranges, including current-month aggregation.
- Define the reporting-side consumption contract: which fields are consumed,
    at what refresh cadence reporting reads them, and any query mechanism the
    metering strategy commits to.
- Record a gap list of anything the schema does not yet provide, and raise it
    with the metering strategy so it can be addressed before that strategy
    lands.
- Recommend how the reporting implementation should integrate with the
    metering data (read approach and error handling for incomplete data), at a
    functional level — implementation details remain with the implementing
    team.
- Confirm timing expectations for when the schema finalizes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written consumption contract exists identifying the exact metering data
  fields the reporting will consume, agreed with the metering strategy's
  owners.
- Each of the three reporting requirements above (per-project attribution,
  GPU-hour quantities, time-range computation) is answered yes/no against the
  draft schema, with evidence.
- Every "no" answer is captured as a concrete gap raised with the metering
  strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990).
- A recommendation on integration approach and refresh cadence is recorded.
- The downstream reporting epics are unblocked or re-scoped based on the
  outcome.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): validates that the metering data can support per-project
  GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges.
- HLR-3 (P1): validates that current-month aggregation is computable from the
  metering data.
- Open Question 1: this epic is the resolution of the strategy's open question
  on metering schema finalization and external timing risk.

# Per-project GPU-hour report computation, reporting API, and CSV export

## Description

This epic delivers the reporting backend for GPU chargeback: computation of
per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over administrator-selectable time
ranges, a stable API through which the reports (and the Dashboard admin views)
are retrieved, and CSV export of those reports for finance tooling. It consumes
the metering data delivered by the GPU usage metering strategy
(RHAISTRAT-9990) per the consumption contract validated by the metering schema
investigation — it must not re-implement usage collection.

## Scope

- Compute per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over
  administrator-selectable time ranges from the metering data.
- Expose the computed reports through a stable API suitable for finance
  tooling retrieval (the API contract is documented and stable across
  releases).
- Provide CSV export of the reports.
- Denominate all reports strictly in GPU-hours (currency/cost-rate modelling
  is out of scope for this strategy).
- Handle incomplete or missing metering data gracefully (per the integration
  recommendation from the schema investigation).
- Integrate into the Dashboard component's existing backend, following its
  established patterns for admin-facing APIs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the metering data delivered by the GPU usage metering work, when an
  administrator requests a per-project GPU-hour consumption report for a
  selected time range, then the report lists GPU-hour consumption per project
  for that range.
- Given a computed report, when it is requested via the stable API, then it is
  returned in a documented, stable format suitable for finance tooling.
- Given a computed report, when it is exported, then a CSV representation is
  produced.
- All quantities are expressed in GPU-hours; no currency or cost-rate
  conversion is performed.
- The implementation consumes the metering data per the validated consumption
  contract and does not re-implement usage collection (metering pipeline
  changes belong to RHAISTRAT-9990).
- Incomplete metering data for a project or range is surfaced clearly rather
  than silently reported as zero.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time
  ranges, computed from the metering data.
- HLR-2 (P1): reports exportable as CSV and retrievable via a stable API for
  finance tooling.

# Dashboard admin views for GPU chargeback reporting

## Description

This epic delivers the administrator-facing Dashboard views for GPU chargeback
reporting: a per-project GPU-hour consumption report view with selectable time
ranges, and an admin view showing current-month consumption against each
project's Kueue quota. It builds on the reporting API and CSV export delivered
by the reporting backend work, and on the per-project Kueue quota data exposed
by the Distributed Workloads component.

## Scope

- Admin view listing per-project GPU-hour consumption for an
  administrator-selected time range, reading the computed reports from the
  reporting backend.
- Admin view showing each project's current-month GPU-hour consumption against
  its Kueue quota.
- Entry point in the view for exporting the displayed report as CSV.
- Restrict the chargeback views to platform administrators (the reporting is
  administrator-facing, not project-user-facing).
- Follow the Dashboard component's existing patterns for admin views and
  navigation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the reporting backend is serving computed reports, when an
  administrator selects a time range, then the admin view lists per-project
  GPU-hour consumption for that range.
- Given the current reporting period, when an administrator opens the
  consumption view, then each project's current-month GPU-hour consumption is
  shown against its Kueue quota.
- Given a displayed report, when the administrator chooses to export it, then a
  CSV is produced via the reporting backend's export capability.
- The chargeback views are visible only to platform administrators.
- Consumption figures shown match the reports served by the reporting backend
  (no independent recomputation in the UI).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): administrators can view per-project GPU-hour consumption reports
  over selectable time ranges (the viewing surface).
- HLR-3 (P1): the Dashboard admin view shows current-month consumption against
  each project's Kueue quota.

# Per-project Kueue quota data for the admin consumption view

## Description

This epic delivers the Distributed Workloads side of the consumption-vs-quota
view: per-project Kueue quota data that the Dashboard admin view can render
alongside each project's GPU-hour consumption. This work is independent of the
metering data — Kueue quota state exists today — so it can proceed in parallel
with the metering schema investigation and delivers the quota half of the
admin view on its own.

## Scope

- Expose per-project Kueue quota information (quota limits and current usage
  per project, per the platform's ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota model) in a
  form the Dashboard can consume for the admin view.
- Ensure quota attribution is available at project granularity, matching the
  per-project granularity of the consumption reports.
- Align with the Distributed Workloads component's existing interfaces and
  conventions (Kueue CRs and metrics); no changes to the metering collection
  pipeline (out of scope, owned by RHAISTRAT-9990).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a platform using Kueue quotas, when the Dashboard requests per-project
  quota data, then quota limits and current usage are available per project.
- Quota attribution granularity matches project granularity (each project's
  quota can be identified for comparison against that project's GPU-hour
  consumption).
- The data is consumable by the Dashboard admin view without custom
  per-project configuration.
- No metering/collection behavior is implemented or altered here.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): provides the Kueue quota side of the Dashboard admin view
  showing current-month consumption against each project's Kueue quota.
